title: Triratna
hook: a Western Buddhist community founded in 1967

segments.voice: Yesterday, Won Buddhism and the plain circle on its altar. Your line was the circle. What round thing stopped you, and who did you meet next? Day one thousand three hundred forty-nine.

A woman walks into an ordination ceremony with the name her parents gave her, and walks out with a new one, a Sanskrit name her aunt will mispronounce at dinner for years. A simple stole now hangs around her neck for ceremonies. On Monday she will be back at her job as a nurse, and on Monday night she will cook for her kids. She has not become a nun. She has joined an order. That distinction sits near the heart of the community she joined. Today: Triratna.
screen: `A NEW NAME AT ORDINATION.` → `BACK AT WORK ON MONDAY.` → `AN ORDER, NOT A CONVENT.`

segments.voice: First, the founder. Triratna was started in Britain by an Englishman known as Sangharakshita. Born Dennis Lingwood in London, he spent many years in India as a Buddhist monk, studying with teachers from several traditions. When he came back to Britain, he found people eager to practice, and he started a new community for them, which grew into what is now called the Triratna Buddhist Community. Second, the name. Triratna is Sanskrit for the three jewels: the Buddha, the dharma, and the sangha, the community. Going for refuge to those three is at the center of the whole movement. Third, the big idea. Triratna has an order, and people are ordained into it, with a new name. But the order is neither monks nor laypeople in the old sense. Its saying is that commitment is primary and lifestyle secondary. A member may be married or single, may live in a shared house with other members or alone, may work in an ordinary job or in one of the community's own businesses. What makes someone a member is going for refuge, not what they wear or where they sleep. The community draws freely on teachings from different Buddhist traditions, and on Western poetry and art as well. Fourth, the hard part. A new community has no centuries of habit to steady it. Triratna has had to face painful accounts from former members about its founder's conduct and about harm in its early years, and it has published its own responses. Building something new means building, too, the ways to face what went wrong.
screen: `AN ENGLISH MONK BACK FROM INDIA.` · `THE THREE JEWELS.` · `COMMITMENT FIRST, LIFESTYLE SECOND.` · `FACING WHAT WENT WRONG.` · then, large: `NEW COMMUNITY.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one community you know that is younger than you are, or close to it: a congregation, a club, a support group, a team, even a group chat. Picture its people. Ask quietly what holds them together. Not the logo or the rules, but the thing they keep coming back for. Then ask what it would need to stay healthy for a long time: what it would need to admit, to forgive, to protect. Breathe with those questions. You don't have to answer them. The bell holds the time.
Triratna. Sanskrit for the three jewels, and the name of a Western Buddhist community founded by Sangharakshita, whose order puts commitment before lifestyle. Today's word.

Your line: new community. Today, notice one group you belong to, and do one small thing that helps it last: a thank-you, a dish washed, a hard truth said kindly. Day one thousand three hundred forty-nine.

howItsDone: Members of the Triratna Buddhist Community go for refuge to the three jewels; those ordained into its order receive a new name and may be married or single, living in shared communities or alone, under the principle that commitment is primary and lifestyle secondary.

fork.setup: you're Sangharakshita, home in Britain after years in India. people want to practice deeply, but few will become monks. what do you build?
options: a monastery, and only monks may truly join.
an order where commitment comes first and lifestyle second.
a lecture series with no community at all.
fork.reveal: an order of committed members who may be married or single, at home or in shared houses: going for refuge, not robes, is what makes a member.

original.note: Sanskrit triratna, the three jewels: the Buddha, the dharma and the sangha.

trapdoor: what you thought: Western Buddhism is just meditation classes.
what it means: Triratna is a community with an ordained order, built around going for refuge to the three jewels.
what a scholar hears: a new form of ordination that is neither monastic nor lay, summed up as commitment primary, lifestyle secondary.

notes: The index hook says 'founded in 1967'; the year is left out of the voice under the claims rule. Earlier name (Friends of the Western Buddhist Order) also left out.
Sangharakshita's biography (born Dennis Lingwood in London, 'many years' in India as a monk, teachers from several traditions): confirm; 'many years' has no number.
The saying 'commitment is primary, lifestyle secondary' is paraphrased as Triratna's own; confirm it is fairly attributed.
The paragraph on harm and the founder's conduct is deliberately brief and neutral; please have it checked for fairness to former members and to the community.
Hook's nurse is an illustration, not a real person; the stole (kesa) worn by order members at ceremonies: confirm.
Editor: softened the hook's overclaim 'the whole reason the community exists' to 'sits near the heart of', and cut the closing stock line 'part of the story of any new community, told honestly'.
